about: VILLAGE-VERNACULAR (docs/VILLAGE_VERNACULAR.md): villages built from a region of the vernacular dataset (src/village/vernacular_regions.json) -- Provence, the Cyclades, the Norse north, Japan -- at both ends of wealth, on flat ground and on real cliffs, then the blends: a hybrid people, two peoples side by side, one region's paint on another's houses, one region's roofs on another's. Each stop is a VillageSpec plus `vernacular` (a plain {region: weight}, or {blend, groups, coherence}). The sidebar names the region and the village and shows VillageVernacularCheck's verdict; a pin's record carries both. Walk: .\visualqa\walk.ps1 -Villages vernacular. Bake first (about an hour): .\visualqa\walk.ps1 -Bake -Villages vernacular

stops.why: Provence: a hill-town market -- ochre, sand and rose render, lavender and sage shutters, canal tile, tall village houses round a Romanesque church
Provence, rich and farming: long low mas and square bastides under hipped tile; the money should show in size and storeys
Cyclades: a fishing village on the coast -- lime-white cubes, flat roofs behind parapets, blue, green and oxblood doors, a blue-domed chapel
Cyclades on real cliffs (Manarola's ground): white cubes stepping down to the sea
Cyclades, poor: a farming hamlet -- small cubes, one storey, the whitewash a little greyed
Norse: a farm village on a stream -- tarred stave longhouses, falu red and ochre log houses with white trim, turf and tarred shingle, a stave church
Japan: a farming village -- minka under straw thatch and grey kawara tile, engawa, dark frames on earth and lime plaster (the church is a stand-in: VERN-JAPAN-LANDMARK)
Japan: a post town on a crossroads -- two-storey machiya, dark timber fronts, tiled irimoya roofs
Blend, one hybrid people: half Norse, half Japanese, each house drawing its type, walls, trim and roof from either
Blend, two peoples side by side: Provencal and Norse houses, each house wholly one or the other (coherence 1)
Blend, one region's paint on another's houses: Provencal houses and roofs, Cycladic whitewash and blue shutters
Blend, one region's roofs on another's houses: Cycladic cubes under Japanese roofing (a mediterranean house cannot build an irimoya, so it keeps its own forms in grey tile and thatch)
